sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1. Rule returnable forthwith 2. Learned APP Mr.K.M.Antani, waives service of Rule on behalf of the respondent State.

3. The present application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for regular bail in connection with FIR being I-11191029220680 of 2022 registered with Rakhiyal Police Station for offence under Sections 376(2)(n), 406, 420 and 294(b) of the Indian Penal Code.
4. Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the applicant submits that considering the nature of the offence, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.
Learned APP appearing on behalf of the respondent-State has opposed grant of regular bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.

sentences.text: 6. Learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties do not press for further reasoned order.
7. Mr.Ramkrishnan, learned advocate for the applicant submitted that the whole basis of the First Information Report (for short, 'FIR') filed against the accused does not inspire confidence.
He has further submitted that applicant as also the first informant were serving together in one Institute and they developed relationship, which may have crossed the barrier of social restrictions.

However,
he has submitted that even assuming without admitting that there were physical relations with the first informant, it is with express consent of the first informant and not on any assurance of any marriage being entered into with her.
He has further submitted that age of the first informant is 35 years whereas applicant-accused is aged about 24 years.
He has further submitted that 'FIR' itself reflects that she is mother of a son even prior to alleged relationship.

It is further submitted that she alleges birth of a girl child out of the relationship through the applicant appears to be incorrect ,
drawing attention of the Court to page 46, which is the birth certificate of a girl child born to the first informant, where name of the father is shown to be one R/CR.MA/2101/2023 ORDER DATED:
21/02/2023 Hiteshbhai Ghoghara.

He has further submitted that the allegation with regard to physical relationship on the promise of marriage also appears to be incorrect as she was already married and having a son prior to this relationship and got divorced.

Despite the same, as submitted by learned advocate for the applicant, it is alleged in the 'FIR' that she became pregnant out of the relationship and she was insisted to get it aborted and despite attempts being made, she did not abort and first informant insisted to marry with her.

It is the girl child, whose birth is registered,
claimed by the first informant to be the outcome of physical relationship with the applicant.
Since DNA Report was not received when his application for bail was heard before the trial Court, it was not considered.

He has further submitted that even the girl child born whose birth certificate is at page 46 to the first informant was abandoned by her and present 'FIR' is an outcome of a case registered against her where she has been exposed to her other relations.
Therefore, it is submitted that the applicant be release on bail as investigation is over and charge-sheet is already filed.
8. As against that Mr.K.M.Antani, learned APP very fairly showed the DNA Report, which is now forming part of the papers of investigation which, prima-facie, helps the applicant in his case.

At the same time, according to his submission, the first informant, who is aged about 35 years R/CR.MA/2101/2023 ORDER DATED: 21/02/2023 and married having a son aged 12 years out of her first wedlock, may be at present she is divorced, and therefore, she is not a person who cannot understand the false promises of marriage.

At any rate, according to his submission, since it is alleged that on false assurance of marriage there was physical relationship with the first informant,
prima-facie, it cannot be disbelieved at present, and therefore, he submitted that the applicant may not be released on bail.

9. Learned APP further submitted that against the present applicant there is one criminal antecedent registered being FIR Part-A 11191021200576 of 2020 registered with Gayakwad Haveli Police Station for the alleged offence under Sections 323, 294(b) and 114 of the Indian Penal Code.
10.

The criminal antecedent shown of the applicant for an offence under Section 323, 294(b) and 114 of the Indian Penal Code would not deter this Court to release the applicant on bail as it appears that Ashutosh Chetanbhai Solanki vs State Of Gujarat on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73731804/
2 offence under Section 323 is alleged without any further details by the Investigating Officer is a non cognizable one and it is only because of Section 294(b), the FIR has come to be registered.

sentences.text: It being mainly non cognizable offence it appears that it is out of some personal dispute with someone else in absence of any further details being R/CR.MA/2101/2023 ORDER DATED: 21/02/2023 shown.

11. Considering the 'FIR' as also the papers of investigation produced for the perusal of the Court by the learned APP, it appears that the applicant as also the first informant are major, they served together for some time in one Institute and might have developed relationship.

From considering the overall circumstances, prima-facie, subject to final decision, physical relationship entered into between the parties cannot be ruled out, but fact remains that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail considering the overall arguments made as also the papers of investigation, and therefore, a case is made out for regular bail.
Hence, I deem it fit to release the applicant on bail.

12. This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in (2012) 1 SCC 40.
13.

entities.text: Sanjay Chandra Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in (2012) 1 SCC 40
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the present application is allowed.
14. The authorities will release the applicant only if he is not required in connection with any other offence for the time being.
If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions Judge concerned will be free to issue warrant or take appropriate action in the matter.
Bail bond to be executed before the lower Court having jurisdiction to try the case.
It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions, in accordance with law.
15. Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.

(UMESH A. TRIVEDI, J) ASHISH M. GADHIYA Ashutosh Chetanbhai Solanki vs State Of Gujarat on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73731804/
